title: Generalized supported class characterized on the modified blowup
statement:
Let $i:Y\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion of Noetherian schemes on which a fixed prime $\ell$ is invertible, with ideal $I$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $E$ be a rank-$r>0$ finite locally free $\mathcal O_Y$-module and $E\twoheadrightarrow I/I^2$ a surjection [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module]. Put $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$, $n\geq1$, with small-etale categories and Tate twists [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist]. Define
$$\mathcal A_a=I^a\times_{I^a/I^{a+1}}\operatorname{Sym}^aE,\qquad B_E=\operatorname{Proj}_X(\mathcal A_\bullet),\qquad\pi:B_E\to X,$$
using coefficientwise multiplication and relative Proj [def-nagata-relative-proj]. Then $\pi$ is projective, is an isomorphism over $U=X-Y$, and $\pi^{-1}Y=P(E)$. The sheaf $\mathcal O_{B_E}(1)$ is invertible and canonically trivial over $U$. If $E=I/I^2$ and $i$ is regular (locally cut out by a regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]), $B_E$ is the ordinary blowup $\operatorname{Proj}_X\bigoplus_a I^a$.
Using the Chern classes of [lem-per-noetherian-etale-chern-identities] and the pseudo-divisor operator of [lem-per-noetherian-supported-product-calculus], put $\xi=c_1(\mathcal O_{P(E)}(1))$ and
$$Q_E=-\sum_{a=0}^{r-1}(-1)^a p^*c_a(E)\xi^{r-1-a},\qquad G=G_{\mathcal O_{B_E}(1),1_U}.$$
There is a split distinguished triangle
$$\Lambda_X\longrightarrow R\pi_*\Lambda_{B_E}\longrightarrow\bigoplus_{a=1}^{r-1}i_*\Lambda_Y(-a)[-2a]\xrightarrow{0}\Lambda_X[1].$$
For every closed $C\subset Y$ the resulting pullback $H_C^q(X,\Lambda(t))\to H_{\pi^{-1}C}^q(B_E,\Lambda(t))$ is injective. For support $Y$ there is an exact sequence
$$0\to H_Y^q(X,\Lambda(t))\xrightarrow{\pi^*}H_{P(E)}^q(B_E,\Lambda(t))\to H^q(P(E),\Lambda(t))/p^*H^q(Y,\Lambda(t))\to0.$$
There is a unique class $\gamma_{i,E}\in H_Y^{2r}(X,\Lambda(r))$ whose pullback is $G(Q_E)$. It has restriction $i^*\gamma_{i,E}=(-1)^rc_r(E)$. For any morphism $v:X'\to X$ with $X'$ Noetherian and $Y'=X'\times_XY$, the pulled-back surjection $E'=v_Y^*E\twoheadrightarrow I'/I'^2$ satisfies $v^*\gamma_{i,E}=\gamma_{i',E'}$. For a surjection $E'\twoheadrightarrow E$ of vector bundles on $Y$ with kernel $K$ and constant $\operatorname{rank}E'=r'$, where $\gamma_{i,E'}$ is formed with the composite surjection $E'\twoheadrightarrow E\twoheadrightarrow I/I^2$, one has
$$\gamma_{i,E'}=(-1)^{r'-r}c_{r'-r}(K)\cdot\gamma_{i,E}.$$
Here the action and the supported groups are those of [lem-per-noetherian-supported-product-calculus]. The triangle, its maps, $Q_E$ and $G(Q_E)$ are natural for coefficient reduction $\mathbf Z/\ell^N\to\mathbf Z/\ell^n$ with the power-map Tate comparison. Regularity of $i$ is not assumed except in the indicated identification with the ordinary blowup.

source.place: Expose XVI, Definition 2.2.1.1, Propositions 2.2.1.3-2.2.1.5, Proposition 2.2.2.1, Corollary 2.2.2.3, Lemmas 2.2.2.4 and 2.2.2.6, Definitions 2.2.2.5 and 2.2.2.7, Propositions 2.2.3.1-2.2.3.2. Coefficient naturality uses the same triangle and Kummer powers at each level.

proof.text: Regard the symmetric powers on $Y$ as modules on $X$ by closed pushforward. The ideal powers and their quotients are quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-times-quasi-coherent-affine-sections], the symmetric powers by the affine identifications of [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra] and the degreewise scalar-base-change identifications of [def-trf-canonical-symmetric-graded-algebra] (each degree therefore has its associated-module affine charts), and their closed pushforwards by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-pushforward-annihilated]. Each $\mathcal A_a$ is the kernel of the difference map from the direct sum to $i_*(I^a/I^{a+1})$, so it is quasi-coherent by the direct-sum and kernel lemmas. The direct sum over $a$ is quasi-coherent by the coproduct lemma. Multiplication of pairs is well-defined because the symmetric-to-conormal map of [lem-pur-conormal-graded-algebra] is a graded algebra map. On an affine open with ring $R$ and ideal $J$, projection $\mathcal A_a\to\operatorname{Sym}^aE$ has kernel $J^{a+1}$ and is surjective: lift the image of a symmetric element in $J^a/J^{a+1}$ to $J^a$. Both end modules are finite over the Noetherian ring $R$; lifting finitely many generators of the quotient and adjoining generators of the kernel proves finiteness of the middle module. Thus every $\mathcal A_a$ is of finite type by the affine criterion.

In degree zero the pair is $(u,u\bmod I)$, so $\mathcal A_0=\mathcal O_X$. Projection $\mathcal A_a\to I^a$ is surjective since $\operatorname{Sym}^aE\to I^a/I^{a+1}$ is surjective (products of degree-one generators span this quotient). The kernel of $\mathcal A_a\to i_*\operatorname{Sym}^aE$ is therefore $I\mathcal A_a=I^{a+1}$: multiplication by $I$ kills the second component and the surjective first projection gives exactly $I I^a$. Hence $\mathcal A_\bullet/I\mathcal A_\bullet=\operatorname{Sym}^\bullet E$. The multiplication map $\mathcal A_1^{\otimes a}\to\mathcal A_a$ is surjective modulo $I$ because a symmetric algebra is generated in degree one. At a point of $Y$, it is consequently surjective modulo the maximal ideal; finite generation from Step 1 and [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] make it surjective on that stalk. Off $Y$, $I=\mathcal O_X$ and $\mathcal A_\bullet=\mathcal O_U[T]$, so it is already surjective. Thus $\mathcal A_\bullet$ is generated by $\mathcal A_1$.

source.place: XVI Proposition 2.2.1.3, second and third paragraphs

proof.text: The symmetric-algebra universal property extends the degree-one inclusion to a graded surjection $\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal A_1)\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal A_\bullet$. By [prop-nagata-relative-proj-functoriality] this embeds $B_E$ as a closed subscheme of $\mathbf P_X(\mathcal A_1)$, proving projectivity in [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism] (not requiring a global free generating set). It is proper by [lem-trf-projective-bundle-proper]. On each affine base open, [lem-sfb-graded-proj-quotient-twist-comparison] identifies the restricted degree-one twist with the pullback of the tautological invertible line on $\mathbf P(\mathcal A_1)$; the latter has the frames of [lem-trf-symmetric-proj-tautological-chart-gluing]. The canonical fraction formulas commute with restriction, hence glue to an invertible $\mathcal O_{B_E}(1)$. Relative Proj base change and Step 2 give $\pi^{-1}Y=\operatorname{Proj}_Y\operatorname{Sym}E=P(E)$. Off $Y$, Proj of $\mathcal O_U[T]$ is $U$, with degree-one generator $T$ trivializing $\mathcal O(1)$; this is also [lemma-nagata-relative-proj-invertible-tensor-powers] for the unit ideal. All these identifications preserve that trivialization.

If $i$ is regular and $E=I/I^2$, choose affine regular-sequence charts. By [lem-sc-regular-ideal-conormal-coordinates], the canonical map $\operatorname{Sym}(I/I^2)\to\bigoplus_aI^a/I^{a+1}$ is an isomorphism there. Projection $\mathcal A_a\to I^a$ now has inverse $u\mapsto(u,\psi_a^{-1}(u\bmod I^{a+1}))$. The inverse preserves products and restrictions, so these projections give a global graded algebra isomorphism $\mathcal A_\bullet\cong\bigoplus_a I^a$. By relative Proj functoriality it gives the claimed ordinary blowup identification, with the Rees algebra of [def-nagata-sheaf-rees-algebra].

Write $k:P(E)\hookrightarrow B_E$ and $p:P(E)\to Y$. Apply [lem-per-proper-modification-etale-excision] to the proper morphism from Step 3 and $K=\Lambda_X$. It identifies the cone of $u:\Lambda_X\to R\pi_*\Lambda_{B_E}$ with $i_*$ of the cone of $\Lambda_Y\to Rp_*\Lambda_{P(E)}$. By [lem-per-noetherian-etale-chern-identities], this latter map is the degree-zero inclusion in the projective-bundle decomposition; its cone is $D_Y=\bigoplus_{a=1}^{r-1}\Lambda_Y(-a)[-2a]$. Consequently we have a triangle $\Lambda_X\xrightarrow{u}R\pi_*\Lambda_{B_E}\xrightarrow{\rho}i_*D_Y\to\Lambda_X[1]$. The map $\rho$ is restriction to $P(E)$ followed by projection away from the degree-zero summand.

Let $e=e_{P(E)}(\mathcal O_{B_E}(1),1_U)$. By [lem-per-noetherian-supported-product-calculus], $e$ restricts to $\xi$, its powers are supported classes, and supported classes are supported-Hom morphisms. For $1\leq a<r$, the morphism represented by $e^a$ and the derived inverse-image/direct-image adjunction of [def-kun-projection-formula-map] gives $s_a:i_*\Lambda_Y(-a)[-2a]\to R\pi_*\Lambda_{B_E}$. The closed-constant pullback comparison of [lem-pur-etale-closed-constant-tensor] and the Tate-line comparisons of [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] identify the sources. Explicitly use the supported-Hom map $k_*\Lambda_{P(E)}(-a)[-2a]\to\Lambda_{B_E}$ and precompose its direct image with the unit $i_*\Lambda_Y\to R\pi_*k_*\Lambda_{P(E)}$. Restriction of $e^a$ is $\xi^a$, so under the projective-bundle decomposition $\rho s_a$ is exactly the $a$th summand inclusion. Thus $s=\bigoplus s_a$ satisfies $\rho s=1$. This splits the triangle: Hom exactness gives a retraction $t$ of $u$ because its connecting map $\delta=\delta\rho s=0$; replace $t$ by $t-ts\rho$ so that $ts=0$. Then $(u,s)$ and $(t,\rho)$ are inverse: their discrepancy on the middle object factors through $u$ by Hom exactness and vanishes after $t$, so is zero. This proves the displayed split triangle, including its zero connecting map.

source.place: XVI Proposition 2.2.2.1, canonical section and last paragraph

proof.text: For closed $C\subset Y$, apply the triangulated derived functor $R\Gamma_C(X,-)$ to the splitting in Step 6; triangulatedness is [lem-weil-pbc-derived-direct-image-triangulated] for the additive left exact supported-section functor. The supported direct-image comparisons of [lem-per-proper-modification-etale-excision] identify its first arrow with $\pi^*:R\Gamma_C(X,\Lambda(t))\to R\Gamma_{\pi^{-1}C}(B_E,\Lambda(t))$. Apply [lem-sbc-ringed-site-perfect-projection-formula] to the locally free rank-one Tate line of [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] to identify the twist of $R\pi_*\Lambda$ with $R\pi_*\Lambda(t)$; the same holds for $i_*$ and $p_*$. Thus Tate twisting gives the same argument with $\Lambda(t)$: its projective-bundle components are $\xi^a$, with source twist $t-a$. A retraction stays a retraction under a functor and under cohomology, hence every displayed pullback is injective. For $C=Y$ the third term is $R\Gamma(Y,D_Y(t))$, since $i_*$ has support on $Y$. The splitting gives a short exact sequence in every degree. By the projective-bundle formula, its third term is $H^q(P(E),\Lambda(t))/p^*H^q(Y,\Lambda(t))$, and its arrow is restriction followed by this quotient, as in Step 5. This is precisely the asserted exact sequence.

source.place: XVI Corollary 2.2.2.3 and following all-bidegree remark

proof.text:
Put $z=G(Q_E)$. Restriction of $G(x)$ to $P(E)$ is $\xi x$ by [lem-per-noetherian-supported-product-calculus]. The Chern relation of [lem-per-noetherian-etale-chern-identities] gives
$$z|_{P(E)}=\xi Q_E=-\sum_{a=0}^{r-1}(-1)^ap^*c_a(E)\xi^{r-a}=(-1)^rp^*c_r(E).$$
This has zero image in the quotient at the end of Step 7's exact sequence. Hence $z$ has a preimage $\gamma_{i,E}$, unique by injectivity. Restricting its defining equation to $P(E)$ gives $p^*i^*\gamma_{i,E}=(-1)^rp^*c_r(E)$. The degree-zero summand in the projective-bundle formula makes $p^*$ injective; cancelling it gives $i^*\gamma_{i,E}=(-1)^rc_r(E)$.

For $v:X'\to X$ put $I'=I\mathcal O_{X'}$ and $E'=v_Y^*E$ with the pulled-back surjection $E'\twoheadrightarrow v_Y^*(I/I^2)\twoheadrightarrow I'/I'^2$, and let $\mathcal A'_\bullet$ and $\pi':B_{E'}\to X'$ be the construction for $(X',Y',E')$; as $X'$ is Noetherian, Steps 1-3 and 7 hold for it. Pairs $(u,e)\mapsto(v^\sharp u,v_Y^*e)$ give a graded algebra map $\phi:v^*\mathcal A_\bullet\to\mathcal A'_\bullet$: the two components stay compatible in $I'^a/I'^{a+1}$ because the surjection for $E'$ is the pulled-back one. Each $\phi_a$ is surjective. Both sides are of finite type (Step 1). Over $U'=X'\setminus Y'$ both sides are $\mathcal O_{U'}$ and $\phi_a$ is the identity. Modulo $I'$, Step 2 for $X$ and for $X'$ identifies $\phi_a$ with the isomorphism $v_Y^*\operatorname{Sym}^aE\to\operatorname{Sym}^aE'$. So at each point of $Y'$, $\phi_a$ is surjective modulo the maximal ideal, and [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] gives surjectivity on the stalk. On affine opens $V'=\operatorname{Spec}R'$ over $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$, let $\psi:\mathcal A(V)\to R'\otimes_R\mathcal A(V)\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal A'(V')$ be the resulting degree-preserving map. [lem-nagata-affine-proj-scalar-extension] and [prop-nagata-relative-proj-functoriality] (3) give morphisms $\operatorname{Proj}\mathcal A'(V')\to\operatorname{Proj}\mathcal A(V)$ over $V'\to V$. On charts these are $D_+(\psi(f))\to D_+(f)$, $a/f^m\mapsto\psi(a)/\psi(f)^m$. These formulas commute with restriction, so they glue to $w:B_{E'}\to B_E$ with $\pi w=v\pi'$ and $w^{-1}P(E)=P(E')$. For $f$ of degree one, the twist frame $f$ goes to the frame $\psi(f)$, and transitions $g=(g/f)f$ go to $\psi(g)=(\psi(g)/\psi(f))\psi(f)$. On the quotient factor this is [lem-sfb-graded-proj-quotient-twist-comparison]. Hence $w^*\mathcal O_{B_E}(1)\cong\mathcal O_{B_{E'}}(1)$, and the section $(1,0)\in\mathcal A_1|_U$ goes to $(1,0)\in\mathcal A'_1|_{U'}$, so $1_U$ goes to $1_{U'}$. Modulo $I'$, $\psi$ is $v_Y^*\operatorname{Sym}E\cong\operatorname{Sym}E'$. Thus over $Y'$, $w$ is the canonical projective-bundle map $P(E')\to P(E)$ and pulls $\mathcal O_{P(E)}(1)$ back to $\mathcal O_{P(E')}(1)$. Chern classes commute with pullback [lem-per-noetherian-etale-chern-identities], so $w_P^*Q_E=Q_{E'}$. The supported Kummer class, its products and $G$ commute with pullback of pairs [lem-per-noetherian-supported-product-calculus], so $w^*G(Q_E)=G'(Q_{E'})$. Therefore
$$\pi'^*(v^*\gamma_{i,E})=w^*(\pi^*\gamma_{i,E})=G'(Q_{E'})=\pi'^*\gamma_{i',E'}.$$
The injectivity proved in Step 7 for $(X',Y',E')$ cancels $\pi'^*$. Only the morphism $w$ is used, not any identification of $B_{E'}$ with the fibre product $X'\times_XB_E$.

source.place: XVI Proposition 2.2.3.1, using the surjectivity argument of the proof of Proposition 2.2.1.5 (Nakayama over U' and modulo I')

proof.text: For $E'\twoheadrightarrow E$ on $Y$, the map on symmetric powers is surjective: locally lift each degree-one factor of a monomial. The resulting graded map $\mathcal A(E')\to\mathcal A(E)$ is surjective too: lift the symmetric component of a pair; its image in $I^a/I^{a+1}$ is unchanged, so keep the ideal-power component. By [prop-nagata-relative-proj-functoriality] there is a closed immersion $j:B_E\hookrightarrow B_{E'}$ over $X$ whose closed-locus map is $P(E)\hookrightarrow P(E')$. The twist comparison [lem-sfb-graded-proj-quotient-twist-comparison], applied on affine opens and glued by its fraction formula, identifies $j^*\mathcal O_{B_{E'}}(1)$ with $\mathcal O_{B_E}(1)$, preserving $1_U$. Thus functoriality of the pseudo-divisor operator gives $j^*G'(Q_{E'})=G(Q_{E'}|_{P(E)})$.

Set $k=r'-r$. In local frames the surjection is a matrix of rank $r$ on each residue field. Shrink to an invertible $r$-column minor; subtract its linear combinations from the remaining columns. The resulting $k$ columns give a basis of the kernel, so $K$ is locally free of rank $k$. For a rank-$m$ bundle $F$ write $S_F(z)=\sum_{a=0}^m(-1)^ac_a(F)z^{m-a}$, $t_F=(-1)^mc_m(F)$ and $Q_F(z)=-(S_F(z)-t_F)/z$; the numerator is divisible by $z$. Include $S_0=t_0=1$ and $Q_0=0$ when $k=0$. Whitney in [lem-per-noetherian-etale-chern-identities] says $S_{E'}=S_KS_E$. Expanding the products and constant terms gives the polynomial identity
$$Q_{E'}(z)=t_KQ_E(z)+Q_K(z)\bigl(t_E-zQ_E(z)\bigr).$$
On $P(E)$, Step 8's Chern relation is $\xi Q_E(\xi)=t_E$. Substitution in this polynomial identity therefore gives
$$Q_{E'}|_{P(E)}=(-1)^kc_k(K)Q_E.$$
Apply the projection formula for the supported action in [lem-per-noetherian-supported-product-calculus], then Step 10, to see that pullback to $B_E$ of both sides of the claimed excess formula is $(-1)^kc_k(K)G(Q_E)$. Their pullback is injective by Step 7, proving the excess formula. This includes isomorphic presentations ($k=0$) and avoids any splitting-principle assumption.

source.place: XVI Proposition 2.2.3.2, universal Whitney calculation written without the source splitting-principle reduction

proof.text: For $N\geq n$ the geometry and twisting line do not depend on the coefficient level. Use the canonical direct-image and inverse-image comparisons under restriction of scalars in [lem-sbc-canonical-restrict-scalars-functor-comparisons]; their units and counits agree by [lem-sbc-restrict-scalars-derived-adjunction-identities]. Thus the natural cone square of [lem-per-proper-modification-etale-excision] commutes with the coefficient morphism. The Chern decomposition and the supported powers $e^a$ defining $s_a$ commute with coefficient reduction by the two calculus nodes. Consequently the maps $u,\rho,s$ of Steps 5-6 commute as well. The coefficients of $Q_E$ and $G(Q_E)$ reduce to those at level $n$. These statements use the power map on Tate lines stipulated in the Chern node, not an identity on roots of unity of different orders. In particular reduction of the defining equation for $\gamma_{i,E}$ agrees with its defining equation at level $n$; uniqueness in Step 8 also makes the classes compatible.
